findings.title: Date override short-circuits the busy-time check
findings.body: When a slot falls inside a user's date override, `dateOverrideExist` is true and `checkIfIsAvailable` returns true before reaching the `busy.every(...)` check at the bottom. A date override replaces working hours, not existing bookings/calendar busy time, so a fixed host with an override 10:00-14:00 and an existing booking 11:00-12:00 will still make the 11:00 round-robin slot pass. That can lead to double booking the fixed host. Only bypass the normal working-hours check for an override; the busy check must still run.

findings.title: Date override check accepts slots only partially inside the override
findings.body: The containment test rejects a slot only when it ends at/before the override start or when it starts after the override end. It never checks that the slot end is within the override end (or that the slot start is at/after the override start). For an override 10:00-11:00, a 60-minute slot 09:30-10:30 or 10:30-11:30 falls through, sets `dateOverrideExist`, and returns true. In round-robin events, aggregate slots generated from another host can therefore be accepted for a fixed host even though they are only partially within the fixed host's override. Require the whole slot to be inside the override.

findings.title: Working-hours end uses the slot start minute instead of the slot end minute
findings.body: `const end` is computed from `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`, exactly the same value as `start`. For a 60-minute slot starting 12:00 when a fixed host's working hours end at 12:30, `end > workingHour.endTime` is `720 > 750`, so the slot is not rejected even though it ends at 13:00. This lets round-robin fixed hosts be booked outside their working hours. Compute `end` from `slotEndTime` (or compare timestamps) and reject slots whose end exceeds the working-hour end.

findings.title: Working-hours check tests only the first matching day and ignores days with no hours
findings.body: `workingHours.find(...)` returns true as soon as it sees the first entry whose `days` includes the slot's UTC day and the slot is outside that one interval. With split availability (09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00), a 13:30 slot is outside the first interval, so the host is marked unavailable even though the second interval contains it. Conversely, if no working-hour entry includes the slot's day, `find` returns undefined and the function falls through to the busy check, treating the fixed host as available on a day they do not work. The check should test whether the slot is inside any matching interval and reject it when no interval matches.

findings.title: Zero-length date override comparison uses object identity
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two distinct Dayjs object references, so it is always false. If a date override with equal start and end is used to represent an unavailable day, that case is never detected; only slots before the override are rejected, and the slot at the override start can be treated as available. Use `.isSame(...)` or compare timestamps.

findings.title: Date override date comparison mixes server-local and UTC dates
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').format('YYYY MM DD')` formats in the server's local timezone, while `slotStartTime` is a `.utc()` Dayjs. On self-hosted servers not running in UTC, the shifted override date is compared to a UTC slot date, so date overrides can be missed or matched to the wrong day. Use `dayjs.utc(date.start)` (and end) for the date/range calculations so both sides use UTC.

findings.title: Active date overrides are filtered by wall-clock date, not actual UTC/invitee date
findings.body: `activeOverrides` compares `dayjs.utc(override.start)`—where `override.start` is the organizer's wall-clock date/time stored as UTC—against the invitee day boundaries. The new conversion below explicitly treats it as wall time by subtracting the organizer offset, but this filter does not. For example, with an organizer in UTC+14, an override at local D 01:00 is stored as D 01:00Z but actually occurs at D-1 11:00Z; when an invitee in UTC views day D-1, the stored value is outside that invitee day, so the override is ignored and normal working hours are used. Convert the override to actual UTC (or to the invitee timezone) before deciding whether it belongs to the invitee day.

findings.title: No test covers the fixed-host round-robin date override behavior or the new availability branches
findings.body: The only added test changes the invitee timezone for a personal event. It does not exercise the PR's main claim: a round-robin event with a fixed host whose date override should constrain available slots. There are also no tests for a fixed host with busy time inside an override, slots partially overlapping an override, or split working hours. These missing cases would have caught the early return that skips busy checks and the working-hours containment bugs.
